$comment: Single source of truth for poly-syntax-highlight grammars. Verified 2026-08-24 (all paths HTTP-checked, licenses from GitHub API). tools/grammar-sync.py consumes this. Two built-in extensions are deliberately left alone despite D5: search-result (the Search Editor's own result view, not a file format users open) and dotenv (poly already ships a community .env grammar as source.env; adding VSCode's source.dotenv would leave two grammars competing for the dotenv language id).

Same upstream as built-in. The two extensions are ours to add: VSCode's shellscript claims neither .bats (bats-core tests) nor .azcli, so both open as plain text with no formatter bound to them, and shfmt parses both as what they are. Adding an association the built-in does not have is not the same as re-declaring one it does -- see build_contributes.

Authoritative HashiCorp grammar. MPL-2.0, ratified by N5: the vendored file is itself the source form and lives in a public repo, which is what MPL-2.0 §3.1 asks for even though sync reserializes it. Keep it unpatched -- a local fix would make us the one owing a source release.

No built-in TOML in VSCode (verified: extensions/toml absent on main). Even Better TOML source grammar (taplo, MIT).

Replaces jinliming2.vscode-go-template; injections into go/html/markdown etc. kept, but never contributed with a language id (injectTo drives them). The main grammar is bound to our own id, not upstream's 'go-template': we declare the language, so a grammar pointing at an id nobody contributes would leave .gotmpl files with no highlighting at all.
mikestead/vscode-dotenv: clean MIT, self-contained plist grammar (converted to JSON by sync).

zxh0/vscode-proto3 (MIT; note: marketplace publisher id is zxh404 but repo owner is zxh0). Bound to our own id rather than upstream's 'proto3' — see the gotmpl entry for what a dangling grammar language id costs.

Replaces bpruitt-goddard.mermaid-markdown-syntax-highlighting. Repo only commits YAML sources with custom !!import tags, so the built JSON is taken from the marketplace VSIX (version-pinned). mdx injection skipped (no mdx here).

Official sveltejs/language-tools grammar. Only YAML source exists in-repo (built JSON generated at package time); sync converts .src.yaml directly — verified via tools/tokenize-check.mjs (96% tokens scoped on fixture). postcss/pug/markdown extras skipped.
Official graphql/graphiql monorepo (vscode-graphql-syntax package). Injections kept for js/ts/jsx/tsx/vue/svelte/python + markdown codeblocks; re/rescript/php/scala skipped.
Generated locally: 16 columns cycling 8 standard scopes (rainbow-csv concept, zero upstream/config dependencies).
Generated locally, tab-separated variant.

Generated locally. The only upstream grammar is textmate/ssh-config.tmbundle, which carries no license file at all, so vendoring it would put an unlicensed file in our notices; the format is small enough to own outright. Any first word is a keyword rather than a closed list, because OpenSSH keeps adding directives and a stale list would silently stop coloring new ones. crontab was considered alongside this and dropped: crontab -e edits a temp file no editor associates anyway.

From CMake Tools, which Microsoft actively maintains; the older twxs.cmake grammar everyone links to has been dormant since 2019. Upstream's filenames entry says CMakelists.txt, which never matches on a case-sensitive filesystem, so the real spelling is used here.
Same source as cmake; CMakeCache.txt is a distinct language upstream because its syntax is key:TYPE=value, not CMake script.
Grafana's Jsonnet extension is the maintained one.
Recipe bodies embed shell/python/js, and the grammar declares those embeddings, so poly's own grammars light them up.
Grammar shipped by the Nix IDE extension, plus its markdown fenced-block injection.

Official Caddy grammar. The caddyfile-test language is a Caddy-internal fixture format and is left out. Upstream puts globs in the extensions array where VSCode only does suffix matching, so the associations are restated as filenames and filenamePatterns.

The section-name alternation is regenerated from systemd docs upstream, which is exactly the churn D4 wants poly to track. The sibling mkosi grammar is left out as too niche. Upstream commits the plist source, not the built JSON.
Maintained by the Scala organisation itself; also used by Metals.
Upstream claims every .conf file, which would fight nginx and systemd for the same files. Narrowed to htaccess-style names and files that live under an apache2/httpd directory.
The Elixir team's own TextMate bundle, which every editor's Elixir support derives from. EEx and HEEx are separate languages upstream and are not taken on yet.
Maintained by the erlang-ls project. The grammar is read from the repo root; Syntaxes/Erlang.plist is a symlink to it and would sync as 15 bytes of path text.
The grammar every Haskell editor plugin derives from. Read from the YAML source: the syntaxes/*.json that upstream's package.json points at is build output and is not committed.

Same source as haskell; .cabal package descriptions are a separate language upstream. Its own language-configuration, not haskell.json: cabal has no {- -} block comments, and offering one made Ctrl+Shift+/ insert something cabal rejects.
From the official OCaml Platform extension. It ships 22 grammars; poly takes the ones an OCaml project actually opens and leaves reason, atd, menhir, cram and the rest.
Same source as ocaml; .mli interfaces get their own grammar upstream.
Same source as ocaml; dune build files are s-expressions, not OCaml.
Same source as ocaml; dune-project has its own dialect of the dune syntax.
Same source as ocaml; opam package metadata.
Jinja templates keep the host language's grammar and add the template delimiters on top, so each host needs its own variant. Poly takes the infrastructure-facing subset of the 28 upstream variants.
See the jinja entry; same upstream, host language html.

Host highlighting only: the yaml grammar opens a document-wide rule (begin \\A / while ^), so the jinja delimiters this variant layers on top never get a turn. Still worth shipping -- without it these files get no language at all.
